business_scope.primary_industry_name: Production and Global Distribution of Vertical Micro-Dramas

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–Hong Kong Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital (2010)
France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1995, as amended by 2009 protocol)
France–Germany Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1959, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L. 561-45 et seq. and R. 561-5 et seq. (UBO register, AML/CFT due diligence); Order No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016; Decree No. 2016-1636 of 1 December 2016; Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed; French Criminal Code Articles 324-1 et seq. (money laundering); Commercial Code Articles L. 123-9 and R. 123-37 on RCS declarations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent registrar extract for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction company registry or Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the home jurisdiction competent authority; if the jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention party, consular legalization by the French embassy or consulate of the document's origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate register extract identifying the register of beneficial owners or shareholders of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction official registry or corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn French translation where the extract is not in French or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (statuts) of the French SAS, including UBO declaration schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notaire public or executing shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a French notaire; for deeds to be registered in France, no foreign apostille is required to the extent execution occurs in France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the local French representative to sign formalities and open the corporate file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorized body of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner and each appointed manager (président)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or notary/competent registration body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization or certification by a French notaire; for foreign-issued documents, apostille/consular legalization and sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives and beneficial shareholders against France's Direction générale du Trésor national freezing list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and French domestic PEP registers. Additional negative-news and adverse-media screening must be run before incorporation and periodically thereafter. Any positive match or unexplained high-risk profile requires a filing with Tracfin under French AML rules. For this ISIC 5911 streaming distribution activity, simplified low-risk customer due diligence may be applied, but exposure to high-risk third-country counterparties will trigger enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RNE and RCS prior name searches via Infogreffe and INPI data.docs
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French corporate names must be expressed in Latin characters; non-Latin names must be transliterated/romanized for RCS registration. There is no official requirement to translate foreign descriptive elements, but the name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or likely to create confusion with an existing protected sign. The legal form must be displayed unambiguously as 'SAS' or 'Société par actions simplifiée' in communications and registers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejection notice from the Guichet Unique must be contested in writing within 15 days by delivering a reasoned opposition to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce where the RCS file is to be opened, followed, if necessary, by an urgent application to the presiding judge of that commercial court (référé) for a decision on admissibility/availability of the name. If the rejection is based on a conflicting registered trademark or prior RCS name, the applicant may alternatively amend the name and refile immediately. No extension beyond the 30-day validity window is permitted after a name is reserved; a fresh availability search and formality is required for a subsequent reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an ISIC 5911 digital-content micro-drama SAS, provided that a valid commercial domiciliation agreement with an approved authorised domiciliary agent in France exists, the agent supplies a physical street address and mail handling, and no actual place of business is nonetheless claimed for turnover-precision purposes. A PO Box is insufficient. Structurally, the registered office can be virtual, but for tax substance and bank onboarding the company should maintain a local operational repository or demonstrate management, records and management decisions from that address on request.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated under 5% annual probability) for a low-risk streaming-only micro-drama production/distribution entity with clean UBOs and no statutory license requirement. Probability rises to moderate (20% to 40%) if the company applies for French tax consolidation, generates substantial French VAT, employs local staff, or presents a mismatch between registered strategic office and actual management activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Livre II, Titre IV, Chapitre V (Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20) governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS); general provisions of Articles L. 210-1 et seq.; implementing rules of Articles R. 227-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, processed exclusively through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire unique de création d'entreprise (CERFA M0) submitted electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.inpi.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital for an SAS (€1 or more permitted); however, at least 50% of cash subscription amounts must be paid up upon incorporation under Article L. 227-2 applying Article L. 225-3, with the balance payable within five years; cash funds must be deposited and blocked with a licensed deposit bank, a notaire, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the RCS registration (Kbis) is obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDER OF [SAS]. The undersigned founding shareholder, acting as sole shareholder of [Company], a société par actions simplifiée in formation, resolves this [date] as follows: 1. Share subscription: the share capital of €[X] is fully subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholder, and said subscription is hereby approved. 2. Registered office: the registered office is fixed at [address], France. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed as President of the SAS with the broadest powers to act on its behalf under Articles L. 227-5 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, effective upon incorporation. 4. Formalities: all filings, capital release, and registration steps with the RCS, INPI, URSSAF, and tax authorities are authorized. Adopted by the founding shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution, and optional notarization of the Articles of Association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholder(s); notaire if notarization is chosen or if in-kind contributions and special benefits are declared
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS statuts in the French language, covering corporate name, legal form, registered office, 99-year duration, share capital, share classes, subscription schedule, President appointment, share-transfer restrictions, and governance rules. Each shareholder must sign the deed. Where non-cash (in-kind) contributions are made, engage a commissaire aux apports to issue the statutory valuation report prior to signing, unless all shareholders validly waive it.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts) in French
Valid identity documents of each shareholder
Domiciliation certificate or lease for the intended registered office
Commissaire aux apports valuation report on in-kind contributions (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies a defect, execute an acte rectificatif (corrigendum) signed by all shareholders and re-certify the deed before submission; if the appointed commissaire aux apports is unavailable, appoint a substitute and re-issue the report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the capital deposit account and certification of paid-up funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed French credit institution, a notaire, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital deposit account (compte de dépôt de fonds) in the name of the société en formation at a French bank or with a notaire. Deposit at least 50% of the subscribed cash capital (or a higher percentage if the articles so provide). Obtain the attestation de dépôt de fonds confirming the blocked amount; funds are released only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract (Kbis) or a certificate of non-registration after the statutory deadline.
required_dossiers: Subscriber subscription slips or bank transfer references
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen bank refuses the account, open the deposit account with another authorized credit institution or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; if the attestation contains errors, request an immediate corrected attestation from the depositary institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the formation notice in a legal announcements journal (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory formation notice to an authorized JAL stating the SAS corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate object, duration, identity of the President, and the rank of the RCS registry where registration is sought. Obtain the attestation de parution (publication certificate), which is mandatory for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final draft statuts (or a certified summary)
Identity of the President and authorized managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the published notice contains an omission or clerical error, publish a corrective notice in the same or another authorized JAL and obtain a fresh attestation before filing the formation dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the INPI Guichet Unique and RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises; processing by the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique portal, complete the CERFA M0 creation form, upload the signed statuts, capital deposit attestation, JAL publication certificate, registered-office proof, non-conviction declaration (attestation sur l'honneur de non-condamnation), and the beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs). Pay the applicable greffe fee online. The Guichet validates completeness and routes the file to the competent commercial registry, which issues the Kbis extract upon approval and notifies INSEE for SIREN/SIRET allocation.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit attestation (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Attestation sur l'honneur de non-condamnation for the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried for incompleteness, cure the defect via the Guichet Unique messaging within 15 days of the preliminary notice; if wrongly routed, request re-routing to the correct greffe; if the greffier refuses registration, petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce for judicial review or resubmit a corrected dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration activation: Kbis, VAT number, URSSAF affiliation, and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF, and the authorized company stationer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Kbis issuance, verify automatic registration with INSEE and the establishment of SIRET codes. Complete the URSSAF affiliation questionnaire within eight days of registration where employees are hired. If the company expects intra-European or cross-border streaming revenue, apply to the local DGFiP business tax office for a French EU VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire). Order the corporate seal and letterhead using the Kbis data.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract issued by the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed beyond the statutory timeline, file a complaint with the greffe and require acceleration; if SIRET or VAT data are erroneous, submit a modification request through the Guichet Unique or directly with the competent DGFiP and INSEE offices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement and DREETS – Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (territorial inspection units); ARCOM for the optional declaration of on-demand audiovisual media services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required – ISIC 5911 digital short-drama production and global streaming do not constitute an Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE); no operating license is issued by the prefecture for this digital activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / DREAL territorial directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – activity not listed under Article R. 122-2 of the Code de l'environnement and not qualifying as an ICPE or SEVESO installation; therefore no full EIA report, no environmental registration, and no prefectural authorization is required for the pure digital production/streaming operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital production; where a physical recording studio or office is operated, comply with: noise emergence limits under Article R. 1334-31 of the Code de la Santé Publique (max 5 dB(A) daytime 07h-22h, max 3 dB(A) night-time); electrical and electronic waste (DEEE) disposal under Articles R. 543-172 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement; and general waste segregation/recycling obligations for office and set waste

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: office and studio premises must comply with Code du travail fire-safety requirements (Articles R. 4227-1 et seq.), including portable extinguishers, emergency exits, fire detection and staff evacuation plans; any area open to the public is additionally subject to ERP clearance under the Code de la Construction et de l'Habitation and periodic commission de sécurité visits. Structural load inspections: obtain the landlord's building-compliance attestation before installing recording equipment, lighting rigs, or heavy server racks; filming sets must be erected only in structurally verified locations. Workplace clearance: prepare and maintain the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP) and register with the occupational health service (CARSAT/PRéSANCE) upon hiring employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — official portals: impots.gouv.fr (tax filing, TéléTVA, professional tax account), formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique for company and TIN registration), and pro.dgfip.fr (professional online services); VAT returns and OSS filings are handled through the DGFiP electronic system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the French SAS (FR_SAS): (1) incorporate via the Guichet Unique, which automatically triggers issuance of SIREN and SIRET identifiers by INSEE; (2) request the intra-Community VAT number (format FR + two-digit key + SIREN) from the DGFiP via the professional online tax account; (3) activate TéléTVA electronic filing for monthly VAT returns. For a foreign entity not established in France: submit Form No. 3557-SD to the competent non-resident corporate tax office (service des impôts des entreprises) to obtain a French VAT ID; if established outside the EU, appoint an accredited fiscal representative (représentant fiscal accrédité) with joint and several liability unless using the Non-Union OSS scheme. For digital micro-drama app distribution, the seller may alternatively register under the OSS/IOSS regimes to declare French VAT on distance sales and B2C electronic services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (an SAS is mandatorily subject to French corporate income tax — Impôt sur les Sociétés, CGI art. 206 — with no pass-through to shareholders; Territorial_Scope: France-resident entity taxed on worldwide profits, with foreign branch profits excluded under the territoriality carve-out and losses of foreign branches non-deductible; Tax_Exempt_Zone: none, standard metropolitan French tax territory applies; Pass_Through_Eligible: no).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SAS has no check-the-box mechanism and cannot elect general pass-through treatment; corporation tax is mandatory. Available elections: (1) reduced corporate tax rate for small and medium enterprises under CGI art. 219 IV-B on the first €42,500 of taxable profit; (2) election for the parent-subsidiary regime (régime mère-fille, CGI art. 145 and 216) for qualifying dividend income; (3) election for tax consolidation (intégration fiscale, CGI art. 223 A) requiring at least 95% ownership in French subsidiaries; (4) election for Young Innovative Company (JEI) tax and social reliefs if R&D expenditure conditions are met; (5) narrow temporary option for income tax (IR) for newly created small SAS under CGI art. 239 bis AA; (6) hybrid mismatch neutralization rules under CGI art. 212 bis implementing ATAD 1 apply mandatorily as a back-stop rather than being elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA), governed by CGI arts. 256 to 298 and transposing Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any taxable economic activity carried out in France by an established business mandates VAT registration from the first euro. Non-established suppliers of B2C digital services (including vertical micro-drama streaming via app stores) must register from the first euro under the Non-Union OSS scheme, with platform deemed-supplier liability under CGI art. 283 quinquies for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing sales to French consumers. EU-established distance sellers of goods benefit from the €10,000 EU-wide annual distance-selling threshold (CGI art. 210 sexdecies) before French VAT applies at destination.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Ordonnance No. 2021-1190, Décret No. 2022-66 as amended): B2B domestic invoices must be emitted and transmitted through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs) or the Public Invoicing Portal (Portail Public de Facturation — PPF) using Factur-X (EN 16931) or structured EDI formats. Roll-out: 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs/VSEs. E-reporting covers international B2B and B2C transaction data transmitted to DGFiP. France does not require real-time digital stamping of each invoice as in Italy or Latin America; continuous transaction controls are achieved through TéléTVA periodic VAT returns and the central PPF clearance repository. App-store settlement data (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, Stripe) must be reconciled against OSS filings or national VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exports outside the EU are zero-rated (exonération, CGI art. 262-I) provided the exporter demonstrates physical removal of the goods from EU territory and retains the prescribed documentary evidence; intra-EU supplies to registered EU businesses may be zero-rated under CGI art. 262-I-1° upon possession of the customer's valid EU VAT number and matching EC sales list filings. Services (vertical micro-drama streaming): digital services follow the place-of-supply rules rather than classic export zero-rating — B2C electronic services are taxed at the customer's location (CGI arts. 259 A and 259 D); sales to non-EU consumers are outside French VAT scope at an effective 0% rate, while sales to EU consumers attract the destination Member State's VAT through the OSS or Non-Union OSS regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU — Document Administratif Unique) or comparable export declaration validated via the DELTA electronic customs system for tangible shipments
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note proving physical removal of goods from the EU
Commercial invoice, packing list, and applicable export permits matching the declared goods and incoterms

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence documenting the repatriation of export proceeds within the statutory period; for digital services: platform settlement statements (Apple, Google, Stripe), customer contracts, content licence agreements, IP usage reports, and app download data
For intra-EU supplies: VIES validation of the customer's EU VAT number and EC Sales List (Déclaration d'échanges de biens) filed to customs
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP applies strict substantive and documentary scrutiny to export zero-rating claims; failure to substantiate physical export or customer location triggers VAT reassessment, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (CGI art. 1727), formal deficiencies at 40% (CGI art. 1728 and 1729-1), abusive tax fraud (manoeuvres frauduleuses) at 80%, and criminal sanctions under CGI art. 1741 of up to €750,000 fine (or twice the sums evaded) and five years' imprisonment. The VAT reassessment window extends to the end of the sixth calendar year following the year at issue (art. L.176 LPF), extended to ten years for hidden activity, non-filing, or established fraud (arts. L.180 and L.181 LPF). Fictitious export schemes, fraudulent intra-EU 'carousel' chains, and misuse of offshore-receivable routing additionally trigger joint and several liability for the scheme promoters and loss of the right to claim refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and payment-services supervision is also allocated to the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, the Autorité des marchés financiers, the European Central Bank, the European Banking Authority, and the French customs and tax administrations as applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange controls or restrictions on conversion between euros and foreign currencies. Current-account payments, including payments for services, royalties, subscriptions, imports, exports, and ordinary profit distributions, are generally freely transferable, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, accounting, and payment-services rules. Capital-account movements, shareholder funding, dividends, intercompany loans, acquisitions, and repatriations are also generally permitted without prior exchange-control approval, but banks may require corporate approvals, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, underlying agreements, invoices, tax support, and proof that the distribution is legally available under French corporate law. A French SAS must satisfy statutory accounts, distributable-profit, solvency, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, and beneficial-ownership requirements before making distributions. Cross-border payments may be delayed or rejected where the payer, payee, bank, intermediary, country, transaction purpose, or goods and services create sanctions, AML, tax-evasion, fraud, or dual-use concerns. Euro payments within SEPA should normally use IBAN and BIC data and are subject to applicable SEPA and payment-services rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a French bank, convert foreign-currency export receipts into euros, or complete conversion within a prescribed period. Export proceeds may normally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the company's commercial discretion. The company must maintain complete commercial, customs, invoice, contract, VAT, accounting, and bank records and provide information required for statistical, customs, tax, AML, sanctions, and banking controls. Foreign-currency balances and transactions must be recorded and valued under applicable French accounting rules. Export transactions may be subject to intra-EU statistical reporting, customs declarations for non-EU trade, VAT evidence, and Banque de France or other statistical reporting requirements where applicable. No universal mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before incorporation, followed by a EUR operational current account and optional foreign-currency accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before incorporation, followed by a EUR operational current account and optional foreign-currency accounts
Capital deposit account before incorporation, followed by a EUR operational current account and optional foreign-currency accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entities
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before incorporation, followed by a EUR operational current account and optional foreign-currency accounts
Capital deposit account before incorporation, followed by a EUR operational current account and optional foreign-currency accounts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for routine collection and payment flows, but not a substitute for a French relationship bank where capital deposit, local credit, cash management, trade finance, or complex treasury support is required. An electronic money institution or payment institution established in France or another EEA state may provide services under its authorization and applicable passporting or freedom-to-provide-services arrangements. A non-EEA offshore EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to French customers merely by being offshore; it generally requires an appropriate EU authorization, establishment, passport, or other legally available basis. Customer funds must be safeguarded and cannot be treated as bank deposits unless held by a licensed credit institution. The SAS must verify the provider's authorization, safeguarding model, settlement banks, client-money segregation, execution location, sanctions controls, data-processing arrangements, insolvency protections, transaction limits, and withdrawal rights. Apple, Google, and Stripe settlement accounts remain subject to their own onboarding, reserve, chargeback, payout, platform, consumer-protection, and sanctions controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank accepts reliable electronic identification, qualified or equivalent signatures, certified corporate records, video verification, and satisfactory beneficial-owner verification. In practice, banks may require a physical meeting, live video interview, notarized or apostilled documents, French-resident contact persons, or an in-person visit where the shareholder chain is foreign, the director is non-resident, the business is newly incorporated, the projected flows are international, or the bank's risk policy requires enhanced due diligence. For pre-incorporation capital deposits, the bank will normally require the founders' subscription documents and identity evidence before issuing the certificate of deposit. After registration, the company must provide its Kbis extract, articles, beneficial-owner filing evidence, tax identifiers, and authorized-signatory mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or multi-layered non-French ownership chain, nominee shareholders, trusts, bearer instruments, or inability to identify the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extracts for every entity in the chain; constitutional documents; shareholder registers; ownership chart showing all direct and indirect percentages and control rights; passports and residential-address evidence for all ultimate beneficial owners and directors; trust or nominee documentation where relevant; beneficial-owner declaration filed in France; certified translations where requested; written explanation of control and governance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SAS with no operating history, limited French substance, remote management, or a business model based on digital subscriptions and platform settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed business plan; management biographies; incorporation documents; office or registered-address evidence; employment and contractor arrangements; platform agreements; Apple, Google, and Stripe onboarding evidence; projected monthly cash-flow statement; customer and supplier geography; pricing model; sample invoices; tax registration evidence; internal AML and sanctions policy; board or shareholder approval of the banking mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained inbound shareholder funding, foreign intercompany loans, capital contributions, or repeated transfers from unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription or contribution agreement; shareholder or board resolution; loan agreement and repayment schedule; lender identity and ownership documents; audited or management accounts; bank statements; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; tax treatment memorandum; payment-purpose narrative; evidence linking the remitter to the shareholder or lender; confirmation that funds are not proceeds of prohibited activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border payments, payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned territories, virtual-asset intermediaries, or unusual payment intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-risk matrix; counterparty master file; sanctions-screening records; beneficial-owner checks; contracts, invoices, purchase orders, customs documents, and delivery evidence; transaction-monitoring rules; escalation procedures; payment approval matrix; explanation of commercial rationale; evidence of screening against EU, UN, French, UK, and US lists where relevant to the transaction or bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared vertical micro-drama production and observed payment activity, including advertising, gaming, adult content, financial services, crypto, gambling, or regulated media activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and content description; platform terms; content-classification and moderation policy; intellectual-property ownership and licenses; distribution agreements; customer terms; refund and chargeback policy; explanation of all revenue streams; restricted-activity statement; evidence that no regulated financial, gambling, crypto, or prohibited-content activity is conducted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high chargebacks, refunds, card-not-present fraud, platform reserves, or concentrated dependence on Apple, Google, or Stripe
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor statements; chargeback and refund reports; fraud-prevention controls; customer-authentication procedures; subscription-cancellation workflow; consumer disclosures; reconciliation reports; reserve agreements; transaction-level audit trail; incident-response records; evidence of segregation between gross sales, taxes, refunds, processor fees, and net settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent tax residence, missing VAT or corporate tax information, unexplained foreign permanent-establishment risk, or failure to provide CRS and FATCA self-certifications
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French SIREN and SIRET data; Kbis extract; VAT number or documented non-registration basis; corporate tax identification; tax-residence certificate where applicable; CRS and FATCA forms; permanent-establishment analysis; transfer-pricing policy; tax adviser confirmation; evidence of filed or scheduled statutory returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, criminal, insolvency, or regulatory findings involving a director, shareholder, UBO, agent, or major counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity-resolution report; independent sanctions and PEP screening; court and insolvency searches; adverse-media review; legal explanation of any historical matter; final judgments or dismissal documents; enhanced monitoring plan; replacement or recusal evidence where risk cannot be mitigated; written bank approval before transaction commencement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through the French bank's pre-incorporation capital deposit account where the SAS is being formed, using a payment from an account held in the subscribing shareholder's name. The payment narrative should identify the company, subscription or contribution, and relevant corporate documents; France does not use a universal statutory FX purpose-code regime comparable to controlled-currency jurisdictions. After incorporation and release of capital, use the SAS EUR operating account for further paid-in capital, share-premium contributions, shareholder loans, and intercompany funding. For each transfer, retain the subscription agreement or loan agreement, shareholder or board resolution, source-of-funds evidence, remitter ownership evidence, bank confirmation, accounting entry, and tax analysis. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments where available and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions, with accurate originator, beneficiary, IBAN, BIC, purpose, invoice, and intermediary-bank data. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third-party accounts, anonymous payment instruments, or an offshore EMI lacking a verifiable regulated settlement structure. Reconcile incoming funds to the general ledger and report any applicable statistical, tax, AML, or beneficial-ownership information.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible EUR suppliers within SEPA, and SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA payments. Include complete payer and beneficiary information, IBAN or account number, BIC or routing data, payment purpose, invoice reference, contract reference, and sanctions-screening information. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a regulated bank under UCP 600, with documentary collections under URC 522 where appropriate. Confirm the bank's sanctions, dual-use, export-control, customs, and country-risk requirements before issuance or negotiation. For digital-content suppliers, maintain contracts, rights licenses, production schedules, invoices, withholding-tax analysis, VAT treatment, and proof of service. Establish dual authorization, beneficiary change verification, callback controls, payment limits, segregation of duties, daily bank reconciliation, and exception reporting. Payment processors and platform settlements should be reconciled separately to gross receipts, refunds, chargebacks, reserves, fees, VAT, and net cash receipts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for forecast or committed exposures, subject to bank eligibility, documented hedging purpose, treasury authorization, counterparty limits, and applicable EU financial-markets rules.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or markets where physical delivery is unavailable or restricted, subject to bank approval, local-market legality, sanctions screening, benchmark and settlement-risk controls, and documented commercial exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for matching foreign-currency funding, receivables, and payables over an approved tenor, normally documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent bank documentation.

Foreign-exchange options and collars may be used where permitted by the bank and appropriate for the company's risk profile, with premium, valuation, early-termination, collateral, and maximum-loss controls.

Hedging must be connected to identifiable commercial, funding, or balance-sheet exposures and must not be used for unauthorized speculation. The SAS should maintain a board-approved treasury policy covering exposure measurement, hedge ratios, counterparties, confirmations, valuation, accounting, collateral, close-out rights, EMIR reporting, clearing or margin requirements where applicable, and periodic effectiveness review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; written shareholder decisions may be used where legally permitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability risk and potential court-ordered approval; no automatic administrative strike-off solely for late approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and related corporate documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique and competent Commercial Court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, daily penalty payment, and fine generally up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; no automatic fixed strike-off deadline, but prolonged non-compliance may trigger registry or court action after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge for late filing or payment, with higher penalties possible for concealment or repeated non-compliance; no automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return or annual VAT summary return, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CA12 return generally due during the second business day after 1 May; monthly or quarterly VAT returns apply instead where the SAS is under the normal VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge generally 10%, plus late-payment interest and possible assessment of tax on an estimated basis; no automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business property tax payment and related local tax compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration and relevant local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally payable by 15 December; annual declarations are required only where specifically requested or where a change affects the tax base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge generally 10% plus late-payment interest; enforcement measures may follow unpaid assessments; no automatic strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant reporting date: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Mandatory appointment may also arise under statutory control, controlled-company, group, or special legal circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables) regulations; IFRS may apply to consolidated accounts or where legally elected or otherwise required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a separate annual UBO confirmation where the registered information remains unchanged. The SAS must file an amended beneficial ownership declaration through the INPI Guichet Unique promptly after any change, generally within 30 days, including changes in ownership, control, or identification data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share-transfer account records
Register of shareholder decisions and approved minutes
Minutes and attendance records for shareholder meetings or written consultations
Corporate officer appointment and delegation records, where applicable
Accounting books and supporting accounting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,000 per year for a French registered office and standard corporate secretarial support; France generally does not require a separate resident registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 4,000-15,000 per year for a small or medium SAS subject to statutory audit; no audit fee is mandatory where the SAS remains exempt

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% corporate income tax rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million (Art. 219-I-b CGI); standard 25% rate on the excess. Audiovisual production tax credit (CIA) of 20% of eligible French production expenditure (30% for animation) creditable against corporate income tax. No statutory year limit for loss carryforward; utilisation of carried-forward losses is capped annually at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above that threshold (Art. 209 CGI). One-year loss carryback option available up to EUR 1,000,000 creating a refundable tax credit.
